Description: Placing, paying for, and cancelling an order — the buyer side of a purchase from a published listing.
Everything a seller does to create, publish, and retire their own listings.
Getting a paid order from acceptance through to the buyer having it in hand, including pre-orders.
Buyers rating and commenting on what they bought, and sellers responding.
A signed-in buyer places and pays for an order from a single published listing.
Cancelling an order before or after payment, with a refund whenever payment was captured.
Creating, publishing, marking out of stock, and restocking a listing.
Retiring a listing for good, from whichever state it happens to be in.
The seller's first decision on a paid order: accept it or reject it with a refund.
Getting an accepted standard order to the buyer, and issuing a digital key immediately after payment.
Accepting an order before its item is back in stock and moving it forward once stock arrives.
A buyer rating and commenting on a delivered purchase, and the seller responding.

Summary: Buyer places a standard order from a published listing
Description: As a buyer, I want to buy a published physical listing so that I can receive the item.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Buying a published listing with stock creates a new order in Created status.
- The order is created for exactly one listing; nothing is added to a cart.
- A guest attempting to buy is sent to sign in first.

Description: As a buyer, I want to pay for my order so that the seller can fulfil it.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Paying a Created order captures payment and moves it to Paid.
- Paying a standard or pre-order reserves one unit of the related listing's stock.
- An order that sells the last unit of a listing takes that listing out of stock.

Summary: Buyer cancels an order before paying
Description: As a buyer, I want to cancel an order I haven't paid for so that I'm not stuck with something I no longer want.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Cancelling a Created order moves it to Cancelled.
- No payment was ever captured, so there is nothing to refund.

Summary: Buyer cannot cancel an order once it's paid
Description: As a buyer, once I've paid for an order, cancelling is the seller's call — I can ask them to reject it, but I can't cancel it myself.
Acceptance Criteria:
- A Paid, Accepted, or Awaiting stock order has no cancel option for the buyer.
- Only the seller can move a paid order to Cancelled, by rejecting it.

Summary: Seller creates and publishes a listing
Description: As a seller, I want to create a listing and publish it so that buyers can find and buy it.
Acceptance Criteria:
- A new listing starts in Draft and is not shown in the buyer catalog.
- Publishing a physical listing requires stock greater than zero.
- Once published, the listing appears in the buyer's catalog.

Summary: Seller marks a listing out of stock
Description: As a seller, I want to mark a listing out of stock so buyers don't try to buy something I can't fulfil.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Marking a published physical listing out of stock sets its stock to zero.
- An out-of-stock listing does not appear as buyable in the catalog.
- Selling the last unit of a listing does the same thing automatically.

Description: As a seller, I want to restock a listing that ran out so it becomes buyable again.
Acceptance Criteria: - Restocking an out-of-stock physical listing returns it to Published with stock available.

Summary: Seller archives a draft or published listing
Description: As a seller, I want to archive a listing I'm no longer selling, whether or not it was ever published.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Archiving a draft listing moves it straight to Archived.
- Archiving a published listing moves it to Archived and it disappears from the catalog.
- An archived listing cannot be published, restocked, or unarchived.

Description: As a seller, I want to archive a listing that's out of stock without first restocking or unpublishing it, since I have no intention of selling it again.
Acceptance Criteria:
- An out-of-stock listing can be archived directly.
- Archiving works the same regardless of which state the listing was in.

Summary: Seller accepts a paid standard order
Description: As a seller, I want to accept a paid order so I can start getting it ready to ship.
Acceptance Criteria: - Accepting a Paid standard order moves it to Accepted by seller.

Description: As a seller, I want to reject a paid order I can't fulfil so the buyer gets their money back.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Rejecting a Paid order moves it to Cancelled.
- The buyer's payment is refunded in full.

Description: As a seller, I want to mark an accepted order as shipped once it's on its way.
Acceptance Criteria: - Shipping an Accepted standard order moves it to Shipped.

Summary: Buyer confirms receipt of a shipped order
Description: As a buyer, I want to confirm I've received my order so it's marked complete.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Confirming a Shipped order moves it to Delivered.
- A delivered order can now be reviewed.

Summary: Seller issues a digital key immediately after payment
Description: As a seller, I want a digital order to skip shipping entirely, since there's nothing physical to send.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Paying for a digital order does not require the seller to accept or ship it.
- The seller issues the key and the order moves straight from Paid to Delivered.

Summary: Seller accepts a pre-order awaiting stock
Description: As a seller, I want to accept a pre-order before I have stock, so the buyer knows I'm committed to fulfilling it once it arrives.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Accepting a paid pre-order moves it to Awaiting stock rather than Accepted.
- The buyer can still see and cancel the order while it waits.

Summary: Seller marks stock arrived for a pre-order
Description: As a seller, I want to move a pre-order forward once stock is in, the same as any standard order from there.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Marking stock arrived on an Awaiting stock pre-order moves it to Accepted by seller.
- From there the order ships and is delivered like a standard order.

Summary: Buyer leaves a review after delivery
Description: As a buyer, I want to rate and comment on something I bought once it's arrived, so other buyers can see how it went.
Acceptance Criteria:
- A review can only be left on a delivered order's listing.
- A review includes a star rating from one to five and a short comment.
- The review appears on the listing page.

Summary: Buyer edits or removes their own review
Description: As a buyer, I want to change my mind about a review I left, or take it down.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The buyer can edit their own review's rating or comment at any time.
- The buyer can remove their own review; any seller response goes with it.

Description: As a seller, I want to publicly respond to a review so I can thank a happy customer or address a complaint.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The seller can post one public response to each review.
- The seller cannot edit or remove the buyer's review itself.
